parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of EnrolmentsController is normal presentation work. It maps HTTP routes, binds the request body to EnrolDto, hands the work to EnrolmentsService and shapes the response ({ refund }). The problem is in the enrol() handler. It checks whether the student email is valid itself and throws a DomainError('invalid', ...). That error type marks the check as a domain rule, which should not live in a controller. The check belongs in the domain layer (the Enrolment entity or a value object) or in the application layer (the service or a declarative DTO validator such as @IsEmail on EnrolDto). Putting it in the controller means any other entry point to EnrolmentsService.enrol skips it. The withdraw() handler only delegates and is fine. Confidence is moderate: plain input-format checks are sometimes accepted at the presentation edge, but raising a DomainError shows this check is treated as a business rule.
